newsitem.title: USA: Rubin repeats dlr been strong for quite some time.
newsitem.headline: Rubin repeats dlr been strong for quite some time.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Wednesday extolled the benefits of a strong dollar but added that the U.S. currency has been strong for a while.
"A strong dollar has resulted in low inflation, lower interest rates in this country and contributed to our economic health," he told reporters after a speech here.
"Having said that," he added, "we've had a strong dollar for quite some time now."
Some analysts have read Rubin's remarks about the dollar, and his recent stepped-up criticism of Japan, as a sign that the Treasury wants to see the U.S. currency lower.

Rubin though denied that his remarks were meant to trigger any movement in the dollar or other currencies. "My comments absolutely, absolutely, are not intended directly or indirectly to call for any movement of any currency," he said.
Turning to the domestic economy, Rubin said that the underlying fundamentals look good for continued solid growth with low inflation.
The Treasury chief stressed the importance of reaching a balanced budget deal for the long-term health of the economy and voiced optimism that a pact would be reached.
"I believe that in the final analysis, the probability is good that we will enact balanced budget legislation this year," he said.

He also said he expects the Clinton administration to nominate its candidates for two vacancies on the Federal Reserve Board soon. "Our hope is that we will have the Fed appointments reasonably soon," he said.
